web.about.daily: Updates are checked once a day.
web.about.lang_problems_hint: These files or lines were not used — English text is shown instead:
web.about.updating: Updating DpiShell… the page will reload automatically
web.adv.info: Off — everything stays as is. On — the listed sites get their own strategy, other sites follow the choice below. “Auto” — strategy search picks the row’s strategy; until then the current one is used. “Direct” — optimization does not touch these sites. Your rows take priority over the YouTube and Discord lists: youtube.com in a row follows that row.
web.adv.others_info: “All sites” may interfere with regular sites — check them after saving. “Direct” — only your rows; other sites go without optimization.
web.core.broken_short: files are damaged, “Restore” is on the “Diagnostics” tab
web.core.missing_long: zapret core is not installed — optimization does not work without it.
web.core.title: zapret core
web.diag.conflict: A similar program interferes: {name}. While it runs, turning on and strategy search are unavailable.
web.diag.flow: Network acceleration (flow offloading) interferes with optimization. “Fix” hands acceleration over to zapret: speed usually barely changes, but on fast plans with hardware acceleration it may drop.
web.diag.flow_handed: handed over to optimization — no interference
web.diag.intro: The router checks what interferes with optimization: similar programs, network acceleration, DNS spoofing. Nothing changes until you click a button.
web.diag.intro_info: Useful when optimization is running but sites do not open, and before asking about a problem. “Save report” collects router and optimization details into a file (no passwords) that can be attached to the question.
web.diag.ipv6: Sites over IPv6 bypass optimization: it is on for IPv4 only. “Fix” turns it on for IPv6 too.
web.diag.ipv6_bad: present — sites over IPv6 bypass optimization
web.diag.ipv6_on: present, optimization is on for IPv6 too — no interference
web.diag.package: Package {name} interferes: another zapret uses the same files. Remove it in the router settings: “System” → “Software” (names may differ) or apk del {name}. Until then, turning on and strategy search are unavailable.
web.diag.report_descr: Versions, optimization and DNS settings, the tail of the router log — as a text file.
web.dns.boot_hint: Needed if the secure DNS address contains a name, not an IP
web.dns.cons1: DNS queries go to Google and Cloudflare encrypted: the ISP usually cannot spoof them, but can block secure DNS itself — then the router switches back to the ISP’s DNS.
web.dns.cons2: ISP filters (such as ISP parental controls) will stop working.
web.dns.cons4: If both secure servers become unavailable, the router temporarily switches back to the ISP’s DNS and warns about it.
web.dns.cons5: Devices with hard-coded DNS (some TVs and set-top boxes) bypass the router — this will not affect them.
web.dns.cons6: Home network device names usually keep working.
web.dns.enable_note: “Revert” restores the previous settings. Turning on usually takes about a minute: the router installs a package and checks that DNS responds.
web.dns.enable_what: For the whole home network. What changes:
web.dns.intro: Some ISPs spoof DNS responses — then optimization may not help apps on phones and TVs. DNS here changes for the whole network.
web.dns.intro_info: “Check DNS” compares the ISP’s DNS responses with reference ones (Google and Cloudflare over an encrypted channel). If responses are spoofed, turn on secure DNS. Browsers with their own secure DNS are not affected. If something stops working after turning it on, use “Revert”.
web.dns.note.default: default: two servers from different companies
web.dns.owner.provider: Addresses come from the ISP, which may spoof responses
web.err.arch: The router architecture is not supported
web.err.boot: Enter the secure DNS server IP
web.err.busy_update: An update is already in progress
web.err.check_off: Optimization is off — nothing to check
web.err.conflict: A similar program is running: {names} — stop it on the “Diagnostics” tab
web.err.doh: A secure DNS address like https://server/dns-query
web.err.doh_or_plain: A secure DNS address or plain DNS addresses are needed
web.err.no_strategy: No strategy selected and no searches yet — run a strategy search
web.err.no_user_sites: There are no own sites on the router — add some or choose other groups
web.err.row_strategy: Strategy: “Auto”, “Direct” or one from the list
web.err.ubus_4: The DpiShell package is not installed or is outdated
web.err.ubus_7: The router did not respond in time
web.main.just_installed: If the package was just installed, refresh the page in a minute.
web.main.off_no_strategy: No strategy selected — “Turn on” starts a strategy search
web.main.reselect_info: On failure a backup strategy is turned on. If backups do not help either — a quick search: 2–3 min, at most once every 6 h; sites on all devices are interrupted meanwhile. That is why it is off by default.
web.main.reset_note: Without this page: on most OpenWrt routers pressing reset for 2 s turns optimization off without a reboot; on some it works differently. Do not hold it for 5 s or longer: that is usually a factory reset.
web.main.restart_note: Optimization will restart — sites will be interrupted for a couple of seconds.
web.main.select_sub: Sites on the network may open intermittently
web.main.stop_confirm: Stop and disable the similar program? It intercepts the same traffic as DpiShell. It will not start after a router reboot; turn it back on in its own settings.
web.main.strategy_info: A strategy is the way optimization tricks the ISP’s equipment; different ISPs need different ones. “Find strategy” shows which one to use: the best one turns on automatically.
web.main.title: DpiShell — connection optimization
web.main.trial_ask: Is everything working? Otherwise the router will revert in {time}.
web.main.ts_info: TCP timestamps are off by default in Windows. Without them some sites may not open from the computer. The DpiShell app on the PC turns them on automatically; manually — in an administrator command prompt: netsh interface tcp set global timestamps=enabled. Phones, TVs and set-top boxes usually need no setup.
web.main.ts_need: This strategy needs TCP timestamps on the computers
web.main.watchdog_info: Every 5 minutes a few regular sites are checked. If they do not open with optimization but open without it, optimization is usually turned off automatically, the reason is shown here, and a strategy search runs once: if a strategy is found it is turned on, otherwise optimization stays off until “Turn on” or “Find strategy”. The watchdog may miss failures on other sites. If there is no internet even without optimization, it is an ISP outage and optimization stays on.
web.msg.deep_none: Deep search: no suitable strategy found. Everything was restored.
web.msg.limited: The ISP seems to be limiting connections temporarily — continue the search later
web.msg.time_limit: The search is limited to 15 minutes
web.select.intro: The router goes through strategies and checks whether YouTube, Discord and your sites open. The page can be closed — the search runs on the router. At the end the best strategy turns on automatically.
web.select.intro_info: Full — all strategies, the best one is chosen; quick — until the first working one, starting with the previous ones. If the ready-made ones do not help, “Deep search” generates and tests new strategies — up to 15 minutes. During the search optimization for the whole network switches several times — sites and games will be interrupted.
web.select.ip_blocked: did not respond with any strategy, looks like an IP block
web.select.mode_info: Full checks all strategies and shows a table — so the most reliable one is visible. Quick — until the first working one. The best strategy turns on automatically.
web.select.warn_off: A strategy search usually takes a few minutes. Sites on the network may open intermittently meanwhile.
web.select.warn_on: During the search optimization for the whole network switches between strategies; sites on devices may open intermittently.
web.site.excluded_hint_main: The list is on the “Sites” tab. The router no longer applies optimization to the site.
web.site.hint: The address is checked with and without optimization. If the site opens only without it, it can be added to exclusions.
web.sites.builtin_descr: Exclusions: sites that optimization interferes with (banks, government services and others). Updated with the package, cannot be edited.
web.sites.exclude_descr: Open without optimization: sites it breaks. One domain per line, e.g. example.com.
web.sites.exclude_info: The line example.com also covers all subdomains (video.example.com). For the domain itself only, without subdomains, write “example.com (this site only)”. Sites added via “Site does not open” also land here.
web.sites.general_descr: Sites that need optimization besides YouTube and Discord. One domain per line. Applies in “Lists only” mode.
web.sites.general_info: Domains from “My sites” below are added here automatically. No need to add sites that already open: there is no benefit, and optimization occasionally interferes with them.
web.sites.mode_all_done: Optimization for all sites except exclusions. Sites will be rechecked automatically.
web.sites.mode_lists_done: Optimization only for sites from the lists. Sites will be rechecked automatically.
web.sites.mode_locked: “Per-site settings” is on — the “Other sites” choice in that card applies to all other sites.
web.sites.targets_descr: Sites that must open besides YouTube and Discord. The router checks them during strategy searches and scheduled checks — for all devices at home. Up to 50 addresses.
web.sites.targets_info: Without an “important” site a strategy is not considered working. Domains from here are added to “Optimize” automatically. If a site stopped opening after being added, remove it or add it to exclusions.
web.uninst.busy: Uninstalling DpiShell… do not close the page
web.uninst.done: DpiShell uninstalled. The page can be closed.
web.uninst.done_kept: DpiShell uninstalled. Settings were kept and will return on reinstall. The page can be closed.
web.uninst.intro: Optimization will stop working on all devices at home. Router settings changed by DpiShell (DNS, network acceleration, schedule) will return to their previous values — your later edits to them may be lost. zapret core and DpiShell packages will be removed; kernel modules and other router packages stay.
web.uninst.too_long: Uninstalling takes longer than usual — refresh the page in a minute.
web.warn.auto_select_failed: Automatic search found no working strategy — the previous one stays
web.warn.dns_fallback: Secure DNS is unavailable — the ISP’s DNS is temporarily in use
web.warn.dns_spoofed: The ISP is spoofing site addresses — apps outside the browser may not work
web.warn.switched_backup: The strategy stopped working — backup {name} is on
web.xfer.backup_saved: A copy of the previous settings is in {file}. To revert, import it with “Replace mine”.
web.xfer.descr: Export to files or import from files: my sites, exclusions, strategies, DNS. The format is shared with the PC app.
web.xfer.dns_risky: A custom DNS server sees and can spoof responses — enable only if you trust the author.
web.xfer.export_intro: Select sections. My sites may be personal — check what goes out.
web.xfer.import_intro: Choose an export folder or a .zip archive. Changes are shown before anything is written.
web.xfer.info: Export is a .zip archive with a folder of text files, one per section. Import accepts this folder or the archive, including an export from the PC. Passwords, logs, statistics and network addresses are never exported. Before importing, what will be added and removed is shown; a copy of the current settings is saved as a file.
web.xfer.newer: The export was made by a newer version — update DpiShell on the router
web.xfer.no_manifest: No manifest.json — this is not a DpiShell export
web.xfer.nothing_in: The package has no sections for the router.
web.xfer.title: My settings
web.xfer.too_big: The archive is larger than 4 MB
